independent_derivation_or_calculation: Independent verification from first principles: 1. Definition: Discrete sum I = sum m_i r_i_perp^2; continuous integral I = int r_perp^2 dm = int r_perp^2 rho dV. Dimensions: [M L^2], SI units kg m^2. 2. Rotational kinetic energy derivation: For rigid rotation with angular speed omega, linear speed of dm is v = omega * r_perp. Total kinetic energy K = int (1/2) v^2 dm = (1/2) omega^2 int r_perp^2 dm = (1/2) I omega^2. Analogy with translational (1/2) m v^2 is exact. 3. Radius of gyration: I = M k^2 implies k = sqrt(I/M), dimension [L]. 4. Geometric distribution comparisons: Thin cylindrical hoop I = M R^2; uniform solid cylinder I = (1/2) M R^2. Both limiting distributions verified.
verification_notes: All physical concepts, integral formulations, dimensional consistency ([M L^2]), rigid-body assumptions, and canonical geometries (hoop vs cylinder) verified from first principles. Distinction between scalar moment of inertia for fixed axis versus full 3D inertia tensor correctly noted in boundary conditions.
findings: Integral and discrete definitions of moment of inertia confirmed dimensionally and physically.
Kinetic energy equivalence K_rot = (1/2) I omega^2 verified via integration of infinitesimal mass elements.
Radius of gyration k = sqrt(I/M) verified with correct dimension [L].
Hoop (M R^2) vs uniform disc ((1/2) M R^2) examples verified.
